chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: A man experiences hadath after he has raised his head from the final sajdah. He said: His salat is complete. The tashahhud is only a sunnah in the salat, so he should perform wudu (ablution), sit in his place or in a clean place, and then recite the tashahhud.

The proper way to understand this report is to interpret it as referring to one who experienced hadath after the two testimonies and before completing the recommended part of the tashahhud. In that case, he performs wudu (ablution) and repeats the tashahhud by way of recommendation. But if it had occurred before the two testimonies, then repeating the salat would have been required of him, as we explained in the earlier reports.

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ الصَّلَاةِ: repeating the salat due to invalidation
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدُ: the declaration recited while seated at the end of salat
key_terms.السُّجُودِ الْأَخِيرِ: the final prostration at the end of the salat
key_terms.الشَّهَادَتَيْنِ: the two testimonies within the tashahhud
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a non-obligatory prescribed practice in this context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone breaks wudu (ablution) after the final sajdah but before finishing the tashahhud in salat?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on one who experiences hadath after raising his head from the final sajdah of salat. It indicates that if this occurs after the two testimonies of the tashahhud, the salat is complete and only the tashahhud is resumed after wudu (ablution); however, if it occurs before the two testimonies, the salat must be repeated. The passage is significant in clarifying the distinction between obligatory and recommended portions of the closing acts of salat.
